• Scientific name: Gagata gagata (Hamilton, 1822)
  • Sometimes inhabits brackish water.
  • Breeding: unreported in the aquarium.

• Synonyms: Pimelodus gagata, Gagata typus
  • Size: 31 cm total length
Asia: India, Bangladesh and Myanmar. Type locality: fresh water rivers and estuaries of Bengal.
Asia: Ganges River basin, India and Bangladesh. Type locality: fresh water rivers and estuaries of Bengal.

Identification: head and body silvery, without pattern. Fins, except caudal fin, black distally, with clear basal portions; caudal fin entirely clear. Dorsal spine extending well past adipose-fin origin when adpressed. Anal fin with 5-6 simple rays, 11 branched rays. Premaxilla with 4 rows of teeth. Most similar to G. melanopterus in coloration and having the highest gill raker counts among its congeners.
Unreported in the aquarium. There is no breeding report.
Etymology: the generic name comes from the local name of the fish (keyakatta). IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2009).

Most similar to G. melanopterus in colouration and having the highest gill raker counts among its congeners. Description: dorsal spines (total): 1; dorsal soft rays (total): 6; vertebrae: 38–39. Head and body silvery, without pattern. Fins, except the caudal fin, are black distally, with clear basal portions; the caudal fin is entirely clear. The dorsal spine extends well past the adipose-fin origin when adpressed. Anal fin with 5–6 simple rays and 11 branched rays. Premaxilla with 4 rows of teeth.

Etymology: the specific name gagata is the local Bengali name for this catfish in India.

IUCN Red List: although there is insufficient information on the distribution, population (and its trends), and biology of Gagata gagata, it is inferred to have a wide distribution; hence Least Concern. Data to verify its supposed decline since the 1800s is badly needed (IUCN 2010).
An account of the fishes found in the river Ganges, pp 197, 379, Pl. 39 (fig. 65).
